audience: A curious New Zealand reader who wants to understand important global developments and learn across politics, conflict, economics, markets, AI, technology, science and geography.
include: Politics, government, public policy, elections, international relations, war and conflict: substantive events and explanatory reporting are relevant without needing an explicit economic consequence.
Economies, markets, monetary policy, trade, business and corporate strategy: concrete developments, mechanisms and well-supported analysis.
AI and technology: capabilities, limitations, research, engineering, security, adoption and governance; include cutting-edge work with appropriate uncertainty.
Science, new research, space, environment and geography: specific findings, discoveries and useful explanations; preserve preliminary-study limitations.
New Zealand and Pacific politics, economies, institutions and regional developments when available in the evidence.
exclude: Promotions, shopping guides, routine entertainment/celebrity coverage and sports results without substantive relevance to an included area.
Isolated crime, accidents or personal tragedy without broader explanatory value; do not misclassify war, diplomatic incidents or political unrest as isolated crime.
Repetitive accounts without new facts; retain their source links with the existing event instead of manufacturing another story.
qualification: Analyse source articles before personal filtering. Retain worthwhile explanatory reporting, narrower developments and uncertainty; relevance does not imply a front-page slot.
ranking: Rank by supported consequence, explanatory learning value and novelty. Importance, freshness and evidence quality are separate. Prefer topic diversity among similarly useful events. Keep relevant lower-ranked stories browsable.
